content: If powerful men and women could center themselves in it, the whole world would be transformed by itself, in its natural rhythm.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching (Dao De Jing), Book of the Way
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

Across his life and work, Lao Tzu saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
